newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end sharply down in brisk volume.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end sharply down in brisk volume.

text.p: Frozen concentrated orange juice futures settled sharply weaker after early speculative selling triggered stops and sent the board to life-of-contract lows, trading sources said.

After failing to gain momentum to the upside over several sessions, the market succumbed to follow-through speculative selling, which pushed the most-active July contract through support at 74.00 cents, to a new contract low of 73.00 cents.
Shortcovering by the trade stymied losses, supporting spot May above its contract low of 72.10 cents, and buoying prices by the close.
"The market is weak technically-speaking and is feeding on itself," Celeste Georgakis, vice president with Dean Witter, said.
The next downside target was pegged at 70.00 cents basis July. Support in May was pegged at 72.00 cents, under which level sell stops are expected to be resting.
The May contract ended 1.95 cents lower at 72.65 cents per lb. Most-active July closed down 1.50 cents at 74.95 cents, having traded from 76.45 to 73.00 cents, a new contract low.
Volume was estimated at a brisk 10,000 lots compared with Monday's official 5,045 lots.
While today's action was technically-driven, a weak fundamental picture continues to dampen overall market sentiment, analysts said.
